facts.fact: The Namibia Statistics Agency states that the Ministry of Home Affairs, Immigration, Safety and Security registers births and deaths and issues the certificates, on the National Population Registration System, whose data the agency obtains from the Office of the Prime Minister, which manages it; no date is given, so the published date is used.

The Namibia Statistics Agency states that a five-year CRVS National Strategic Plan for 2015/16 to 2020/21 was approved by Cabinet in 2015, following the 2014 comprehensive assessment, with national steering and technical committees set up to implement it; the report names no later plan.

The Namibia Statistics Agency reports births and deaths registered and captured on the NPRS in 2018 to 2021 (85,853 births and 24,388 deaths registered in 2021, from records captured up to 17 February 2022); marriages are captured on it at head office only, since 2014.

The Namibia Statistics Agency states that applications are processed and captured onto the NPRS and certificates issued by the local civil registration office, with registration at national, regional and sub-regional level and at most district hospitals and the information available in real time across the 14 regions; capture is delayed at some remote offices lacking computers or internet, and paper records are still couriered to head office for archiving. No date is given, so the published date is used.

The Namibia Statistics Agency reports that the share of registered births captured on the NPRS within 14 days fell from 87.1 per cent in 2018 to 68.9 per cent in 2021, while deaths captured within 14 days rose from 58.0 to 89.6 per cent; 96.2 per cent of births and 92.5 per cent of deaths were captured within 12 months in 2021.

The Namibia Statistics Agency states that some registration offices in remote areas lack computers or internet connectivity, so that capture of records on the NPRS may be delayed; it gives no count of offices, with or without the system. No date is given, so the published date is used.
